review.summary: Scoped follow-up review of the repairs only. This is not release certification: DB and browser checks were not run because Docker Desktop could not start. Prior MINOR1 is fixed. Both entrances now pass the `!runtime` / `unavailable` → `notFound()` gate before building the retry boundary. The root page builds the boundary lazily through `buildRetryBoundary`, and the step page builds it after the gate. Prior MINOR2 is mostly fixed. New tests cover unrecognised, recognised and array-valued retry queries, closed/redirect entrances, and the null/unavailable runtime gate. Closing the prior NIT is consistent with the string-only Zod schema for `Answers`. One minor test gap remains: the page-level `next/headers` mock leaves out `headers`. So the draft-display and verified-submission paths can't run on expired entrances, and the 'never read retry evidence' assertions can't detect anything on their own. I found no new production defects in the changed files.

findings.area: vi.mock("next/headers") and the expired-entrance / availability-gate tests
findings.issue: The `next/headers` mock provides only `cookies`, not `headers`. In `registrationRetryBoundary` and `verifiedRegistrationSubmission`, `(await headers())` therefore throws a TypeError before `readRegistrationRetryDraft` or `verifyRegistrationResult` is ever called. As a result: (a) the expired-entrance tests can only use `registrationRetry: "unavailable"`, the one value that skips the cookie/draft path, so the read-only draft fields and the verified-submission status on closed/redirect pages are never tested end to end; (b) in the availability-gate test, `expect(mocks.readDraft).not.toHaveBeenCalled()` and `expect(mocks.verifyResult).not.toHaveBeenCalled()` can never fail. If the order were reversed, the error would come from the missing `headers` mock, not from the draft read.
findings.evidence: `vi.mock("next/headers", () => ({ cookies: vi.fn(async () => ...) }))` has no `headers` export. The boundary calls `(await headers()).get("host")` before `readRegistrationRetryDraft(...)`, and `verifiedRegistrationSubmission` calls `headers()` before `verifyRegistrationResult(...)`. The expired-entrance test uses only `{registrationRetry:"unavailable"}`.
findings.impact: An ordering regression would still make the gate test fail, but through an unrelated TypeError rather than the intended assertion. A regression that leaks or drops the read-only draft, or the verified-result message, on the closed/redirect entrances would not be caught by unit tests. Real DB/browser checks are also blocked right now.
findings.recommended_fix: Add `headers: vi.fn(async () => new Headers({ host: "example.test" }))` to the `next/headers` mock. Then extend the expired-entrance test with a `registrationRetry: "429"` case where `mocks.readDraft` resolves a draft (e.g. `{ answers: { email: "a@example.test" }, ... }`), and a `submitted: "verification_required"` case where `mocks.verifyResult` resolves `true`.
findings.required_test: For both closed and redirect, on both the root and step entrances: (1) retry=429 with a mocked draft renders a `readOnly` input with the draft value and no `<form`; (2) submitted=verification_required with verifyResult=true renders FORM_SUBMISSION_VERIFICATION_MESSAGE; (3) the availability-gate test, with `headers` mocked, still rejects with NOT_FOUND and readDraft/verifyResult are not called. Check that (3) fails if `registrationRetryBoundary` is moved back before the gate.
